items.description: Sec. 4 says only '20 × 60 finite-element grid' and never says which number runs horizontally. Two hints point to a landscape domain: Sec. 5.1 says the right-edge load gives a design using 'the complete horizontal domain', and Table A.5 calls a Top88 setup '20 × 60 half-MBB' (normally nelx=60, nely=20). Neither is stated outright for this problem.
readings: 60 elements horizontal × 20 vertical (nelx=60, nely=20; span:height = 3:1; supported left edge is the short side)
20 elements horizontal × 60 vertical (nelx=20, nely=60; span:height = 1:3; supported left edge is the long side)

items.entity: unit downward load on the right edge
items.description: Sec. 4 puts the load on a 'randomly selected admissible node on the lower, upper, or right boundary region' and never defines 'admissible'; it may exclude corners. Sec. 5.1 says only that the Fig. 5(c) case has 'right-edge loading'. Which node on the right edge is loaded can only be seen in Fig. 5(c).

items.entity: load applied at a node vs. an element
items.description: Sec. 4 applies the unit load to an 'admissible node', but Sec. 2.2 / Eq. 5 says the load channel is 'nonzero at the loaded element'. It is unclear whether the FE load is a single nodal force or a unit force spread over the nodes of one element.
readings: single nodal point force Fy = -1 at one right-edge node
total Fy = -1 split equally over the two right-edge nodes of the loaded boundary element (-0.5 each)
total Fy = -1 split over the four nodes of the loaded element (-0.25 each)

items.entity: target volume fraction of the Fig. 5(c) shared problem
items.description: Sec. 4 says only that dataset volume fractions are drawn uniformly from [0.3, 0.7]. Sec. 5.1 and the Fig. 5(c) caption say the volume target is the same in every row but never give it; at best it could be estimated from the grey level of the ρinit panel. The value 0.5 in Table A.5 belongs to a different (half-MBB) setup.

items.entity: solid Young's modulus E0 and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Eq. 2 uses E0 but no value is given anywhere, and neither is the element thickness. The Fig. 5(c) panel titles report absolute compliance C, which depends on both.
readings: physical modulus, e.g. E0 = 210 GPa (steel), unit thickness; compliance scales as 1/E0

items.entity: void stiffness Emin / lower density bound
items.description: Eq. 2 uses a modified SIMP law with Emin but gives no value. Sec. 4 clips initial densities to [0.001, 1.0], which hints at a 99-line-style lower density bound of 0.001. Emin also sets the compliance of the thresholded designs used for the reported ratios.
readings: Emin = 1e-9·E0 with ρ in [0,1] (Top88 modified SIMP)
Emin = 1e-3·E0, i.e. ρmin = 0.001 (99-line style, matches the init clipping)

items.description: Neither the Poisson's ratio nor plane stress vs. plane strain is stated anywhere. The only hint is that Sec. 3.1 / A.5 refer to a 'Top88/SIMP optimizer', whose code uses ν = 0.3 in plane stress.

Sec. 2.1 says only that sensitivities are 'regularized via standard convolution filtering [3,4]'. No radius is given for the SIMP runs that produced the dataset and reference designs, and no physical element size is given that would let a radius in length units be converted.

Sec. 2.1 says 'standard convolution filtering [3,4]' is applied to the 'adjoint compliance sensitivities'. Ref. [4] contains both the sensitivity filter and the density filter, and the kernel shape is not stated.
readings: sensitivity filter (Top88 ft=1, linear cone weights, density-weighted)
density filter (Top88 ft=2) with chain-rule sensitivities

items.description: Sec. 2.1 cites OC updates [31] but gives no move limit, damping exponent or bisection tolerance. Because SIMP is non-convex (Sec. 1), these can steer the run to a different local optimum.

No convergence tolerance or maximum iteration count is given for the dataset/reference SIMP runs. Table A.5 (a different experiment) shows non-converged runs stopping at 100 iterations and the baseline converging at 94, which hints at Top88 defaults with a 100-iteration cap.
readings: stop when max|Δρ| < 0.01 or after 100 iterations
stop when max|Δρ| < 0.01 or after 200 iterations

items.entity: starting density field of the reference SIMP run
items.description: Sec. 4 builds ρinit as the target volume fraction plus 'Gaussian-smoothed random variation with amplitude 0.05', clipped to [0.001, 1]. It gives no smoothing width, noise type, seed, or mean renormalization, and does not say whether 0.05 is a standard deviation or a peak. Sec. 5.4 implies the clean reference run starts from this field rather than a uniform one, but never says so. The actual field appears only in column 1 of Fig. 5(c).
readings: uniform ρ = Vf everywhere (standard Top88 start)
Vf + white noise Gaussian-smoothed (σ ≈ 2 elements) and scaled to std 0.05, clipped to [0.001, 1]
Vf + smoothed noise scaled to peak |δ| = 0.05, clipped to [0.001, 1]
ρinit field digitized from Fig. 5(c), column 1

items.entity: compliance evaluation of the SIMP reference (thresholding)
items.description: Sec. 5.1 and the Fig. 5(b)/(c) captions report 'thresholded' compliance ratios, and the absolute C appears only in the panel titles. The text does not say whether the SIMP/GT compliance is computed on the grey field or a binarized one, nor what threshold is used or what stiffness void elements get.
readings: compliance of the grey (unthresholded) SIMP density field
binarize at ρ ≥ 0.5 (void elements set to Emin), then compute C
binarize at the volume-preserving threshold (densest Vf fraction solid), then compute C

items.description: Sec. 4 gives only the 20 × 60 grid size. The element type, integration rule and element aspect ratio / physical size are never stated.
readings: square unit-size 4-node bilinear (Q4) elements with the Top88 element stiffness matrix
